criterion: which type of entity the encyclopedia article describes

categories.name: Person
categories.definition: An individual human being, including artists, politicians, athletes, and other notable figures.

categories.name: Company
categories.definition: A business or organization that produces goods or provides services.

categories.name: Plant
categories.definition: A living organism of the kind exemplified by trees, shrubs, herbs, grasses, ferns, and mosses, typically growing in a permanent site.

categories.name: Animal
categories.definition: A living organism that feeds on organic matter, typically having specialized sense organs and nervous system and able to respond rapidly to stimuli.

categories.name: Film
categories.definition: A motion picture or movie, including documentaries and feature films.

categories.name: Book
categories.definition: A written or printed work consisting of pages glued or sewn together along one side and bound in covers.

categories.name: Music Album
categories.definition: A collection of audio recordings issued as a single item on CD, record, or another medium.

categories.name: Song
categories.definition: A short piece of music with words that are sung.

categories.name: Village
categories.definition: A small community or group of houses in a rural area, larger than a hamlet and usually smaller than a town.

categories.name: City
categories.definition: A large town or a significant urban area.

categories.name: River
categories.definition: A large natural stream of water flowing in a channel to the sea, a lake, or another river.

categories.name: Mountain
categories.definition: A large natural elevation of the earth's surface rising abruptly from the surrounding level.

categories.name: Lake
categories.definition: A large body of water surrounded by land.

categories.name: Building
categories.definition: A structure with a roof and walls, such as a house, school, or factory.

categories.name: School
categories.definition: An institution for educating children or a place where people go to learn a particular subject.

categories.name: University
categories.definition: An institution of higher education and research which awards academic degrees in various academic disciplines.

categories.name: Historical Event
categories.definition: A significant occurrence or happening in history.

categories.name: Vehicle
categories.definition: A thing used for transporting people or goods, especially on land, such as a car, truck, or cart.

categories.name: Ship
categories.definition: A large watercraft that travels the world's oceans and other sufficiently deep waterways, carrying passengers or goods.

categories.name: Aircraft
categories.definition: A vehicle that is able to fly by gaining support from the air, or in general, the atmosphere of a planet.

categories.name: Organization
categories.definition: An organized group of people with a particular purpose, such as a business or government department.

categories.name: Journal
categories.definition: A newspaper or magazine that deals with a particular subject or professional activity.

categories.name: Magazine
categories.definition: A periodical publication containing articles and illustrations, often on a particular subject or aimed at a particular readership.

categories.name: Newspaper
categories.definition: A printed publication (usually issued daily or weekly) consisting of folded unstapled sheets and containing news, articles, advertisements, and correspondence.

categories.name: Sport
categories.definition: An activity involving physical exertion and skill in which an individual or team competes against another or others for entertainment.

categories.name: Game
categories.definition: A form of play or sport, especially a competitive one played according to rules and decided by skill, strength, or luck.

categories.name: Art
categories.definition: The expression or application of human creative skill and imagination, typically in a visual form such as painting or sculpture.

categories.name: Technology
categories.definition: The application of scientific knowledge for practical purposes, especially in industry.

categories.name: Government
categories.definition: The governing body of a nation, state, or community.

categories.name: Religion
categories.definition: A particular system of faith and worship.

categories.name: Mythology
categories.definition: A collection of myths, especially one belonging to a particular religious or cultural tradition.

categories.name: Science
categories.definition: The intellectual and practical activity encompassing the systematic study of the structure and behavior of the physical and natural world through observation and experiment.

categories.name: Animal Species
categories.definition: A group of living organisms consisting of similar individuals capable of exchanging genes or interbreeding.

categories.name: Plant Species
categories.definition: A group of plants that are similar and can interbreed.

categories.name: Insect
categories.definition: A small arthropod animal that has six legs and generally one or two pairs of wings.

categories.name: Bird
categories.definition: A warm-blooded egg-laying vertebrate animal distinguished by the possession of feathers, wings, and a beak and (typically) by being able to fly.

categories.name: Reptile
categories.definition: A cold-blooded, egg-laying vertebrate of a class that includes snakes, lizards, crocodiles, turtles, and tortoises.

categories.name: Amphibian
categories.definition: A cold-blooded vertebrate animal of a class that comprises the frogs, toads, newts, and salamanders.

categories.name: Fish
categories.definition: A limbless cold-blooded vertebrate animal with gills and fins living wholly in water.

categories.name: Mammal
categories.definition: A warm-blooded vertebrate animal of a class that is distinguished by the possession of hair or fur, the secretion of milk by females for the nourishment of the young, and (typically) the birth of live young.

categories.name: Invertebrate
categories.definition: An animal lacking a backbone, such as an arthropod, mollusk, annelid, coelenterate, etc.

categories.name: Fungus
categories.definition: Any of a group of spore-producing organisms feeding on organic matter, including molds, yeast, mushrooms, and toadstools.

categories.name: Mineral
categories.definition: A solid inorganic substance of natural occurrence.

categories.name: Chemical
categories.definition: A compound or substance that has been purified or prepared, especially artificially.

categories.name: Astronomical Object
categories.definition: A naturally occurring physical entity, association, or structure that exists in the observable universe.

categories.name: Event
categories.definition: A thing that happens, especially one of importance.

categories.name: Festival
categories.definition: A day or period of celebration, typically for religious reasons.

categories.name: Holiday
categories.definition: A day of festivity or recreation when no work is done.

categories.name: Language
categories.definition: The method of human communication, either spoken or written, consisting of the use of words in a structured and conventional way.

categories.name: Cuisine
categories.definition: A style or method of cooking, especially as characteristic of a particular country, region, or establishment.
